## Summary of PR/Issue
PR #380 implements issue #375’s request to stop leaving Sepo’s model quality floor to ACPX/provider defaults. It adds small built-in provider defaults for Codex and Claude in `resolve-agent-provider`, preserves `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` and inline route override precedence, and updates operator-facing docs. The linked issue asked for a minimal implementation: pin good defaults without turning Sepo into a full model catalog. The current implementation covers single-agent provider resolution and review synthesis, but not the direct Claude/Codex reviewer lanes.

## Review
The core resolver change is small and aligned with the requested minimal-defaults boundary. One unresolved gap remains: review lanes are still Sepo-owned default model runs, but they bypass the new pinned default path.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Reviewer lanes remain on provider defaults | BLOCKING | `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` still calls `run-agent-task` for Claude/Codex reviewer lanes without a `model`, while the new defaults only flow through `resolve-agent-provider`. This leaves a major Sepo-owned model path unpinned despite the PR’s goal. |

## Progress
- Resolver defaults now pin `codex` to `gpt-5.5` and `claude` to `claude-sonnet-4-6`.
- Existing policy and inline override precedence is preserved, and targeted resolver/docs coverage was added.
- Rubrics review passed and the alternate Claude review considered the remaining coverage/doc notes non-blocking.
- Posted one inline comment on `.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md` line 64 for the reviewer-lane gap.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Reviewer lanes remain on provider defaults</summary>

**Cause:** The PR adds built-in defaults inside `resolve-agent-provider`, but the review matrix directly invokes `run-agent-task` with `agent: ${{ matrix.agent }}` and `reasoning_effort` only. The synthesis job uses the resolver, but the Claude/Codex reviewer jobs still rely on ACPX/provider defaults.

**Candidate solutions:** Add explicit model entries to the reviewer matrix and pass `model: ${{ matrix.model }}`, or run each reviewer lane through `resolve-agent-provider` with the provider fixed by the matrix lane so the same built-in defaults are applied.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed on severity: one review marked this blocking, while the Claude and rubrics reviews treated the PR as shippable. I’m treating it as blocking because issue #375 asked to pin good Sepo defaults, and these reviewer lanes are still default Sepo agent runs.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
`FIX_PR`: The remaining issue is a concrete branch change suitable for automation: pin or resolver-derive models for the review lane matrix before the PR claims Sepo defaults are pinned.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Ensure the Claude and Codex reviewer lanes pass pinned model IDs, either via explicit matrix `model` values or by resolving each lane through `resolve-agent-provider` with the lane provider fixed.

@sepo-agent /answer 

Please fix to use opus 4.8 by default rather than sonnet; also refer to latest models. Further, I was wondering what's a better architecture fix? 

For example, we can host the model names on a static site etc; and it can call the static site for the names and fall back to some default values (such that we can avoid resorting to the hard coded names in the codebase?

I can’t push code from the `/answer` route, but the concrete PR fix is small:

- Change the Claude built-in default in [`resolve-provider.js`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fe55695c0d410c95db26e39973eabfe8259e2fbc/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.js#L8-L12) from `claude-sonnet-4-6` to `claude-opus-4-8`.
- Update the matching resolver test expectation in [`resolve-agent-provider.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fe55695c0d410c95db26e39973eabfe8259e2fbc/.agent/src/__tests__/resolve-agent-provider.test.ts#L117-L134).
- Update docs/examples in [`configuration-list.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fe55695c0d410c95db26e39973eabfe8259e2fbc/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L40-L64) and any other references to the Claude default.
- Keep the review workflow as-is structurally: it already routes reviewer lanes through `resolve-agent-provider`, so changing the resolver default will flow into Claude review lanes via [`agent-review.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fe55695c0d410c95db26e39973eabfe8259e2fbc/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L167-L208).

I checked the current docs: Anthropic lists `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, and `claude-haiku-4-5` as the latest comparison set, and says `opus` resolves to Opus 4.8 on the Anthropic API. It also says Opus 4.8 requires Claude Code `v2.1.154` or later, so the fix should either document that runner requirement or add a Claude CLI version check/upgrade path. Sources: [Claude models overview](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview), [Claude Code model config](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config). OpenAI currently lists `gpt-5.5` as the frontier/default complex-work model, so the Codex side of PR #380 looks aligned with latest docs: [OpenAI GPT-5.5](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.5).

For the architecture: I would not make every agent run fetch model names from a static site by default. That makes CI behavior nondeterministic, adds a runtime network dependency, and lets defaults change outside the repo’s review/release process.

Better architecture:

1. Keep a tiny versioned model-defaults manifest in this repo, not inline in code.
   Example: `.agent/model-defaults.json` with `codex.default`, `claude.default`, `cheap`, `strong`, `min_cli_version`, `source_url`, and `verified_at`.

2. Have `resolve-agent-provider` read that manifest, with hardcoded emergency fallback only if the manifest is missing or invalid.

3. Keep `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY` as the user override layer. Repo owners should always be able to pin a different model without waiting for Sepo.

4. Add a manual/scheduled “model defaults check” workflow that consults official provider docs/APIs and opens a PR when curated defaults are stale. That is where a static hosted recommendation feed could help.

5. If we use a static site, use it only as an update signal, not as the runtime source of truth. Runtime should stay pinned, auditable, and reproducible.

So my recommended next branch change is: switch Claude default to `claude-opus-4-8` now, add the Claude Code minimum-version caveat, then follow up with a small manifest-based refactor rather than a live remote lookup.

> Keep a tiny versioned model-defaults manifest in this repo, not inline in code.
> Example: .agent/model-defaults.json with codex.default, claude.default, cheap, strong, min_cli_version, source_url, and verified_at.

There are two levels of questions here: 
1. ok for this repo, yes, it makes sense. But for other repo that installs/ based on our current sepo infra), they might not update it that frequently (perhaps solved after #383 ); therefore it's kinda cumbersome 
2. or for installed repos, others can use the github raw url for the model name json registry and then fall back to the defaults?

Yes, I think the installed-repo concern changes the design.

For the source repo, a versioned `.agent/model-defaults.json` is enough. For installed repos, relying only on copied files means model defaults age until `agent-update.yml` runs and the update PR is merged. #383 helps by making update cadence less stale/noisy, but it still depends on repo owners accepting infra update PRs.

So I’d use a layered model source:

1. **Bundled defaults**: shipped with installed Sepo infra.
2. **Remote Sepo registry**: optional/default curated JSON from `self-evolving/repo`, fetched at runtime with a short timeout.
3. **Repo-owned overrides**: `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`, always highest precedence.

Precedence should be:

```text
bundled Sepo defaults
< remote Sepo model registry, if enabled and valid
< AGENT_MODEL_POLICY.default / providers / route_overrides
< inline workflow route_provider/provider escape hatches
```

Using GitHub raw can work, but I’d make it boring and constrained:

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/self-evolving/repo/<stable-ref>/.agent/model-defaults.json
```

Not arbitrary remote URLs by default. Arbitrary URLs are a supply-chain footgun for CI. If we allow them, put them behind an explicit variable like `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY_URL`.

Suggested config surface:

- `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY=auto|bundled|remote`
  - `auto`: try Sepo’s registry, fall back to bundled.
  - `bundled`: fully deterministic/offline.
  - `remote`: require remote registry, but still fail closed to bundled unless we intentionally want hard failure.
- `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY_URL`: optional custom registry URL.
- `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`: local override, still wins.

Runtime rules:

- Fetch with a short timeout, maybe 2-5 seconds.
- Validate schema strictly.
- Accept only known providers: `codex`, `claude`.
- Accept only safe model/reasoning tokens using the existing resolver token validation.
- Log whether the model came from `bundled`, `remote`, or `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`.
- Never let remote defaults override repo-local `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`.

I would not make model names only hardcoded in JS. The better fix is:

- Move defaults into `.agent/model-defaults.json`.
- Teach [`resolve-agent-provider`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.js) to load bundled JSON, then optionally remote JSON, then policy.
- Keep `agent-update.yml` as the durable infra update path, but let model defaults refresh between infra updates through the remote registry.

That gives installed repos fresher defaults without forcing frequent Sepo infra updates, while preserving reproducibility and local override control.

> Yes, I think the installed-repo concern changes the design.
> 
> For the source repo, a versioned `.agent/model-defaults.json` is enough. For installed repos, relying only on copied files means model defaults age until `agent-update.yml` runs and the update PR is merged. #383 helps by making update cadence less stale/noisy, but it still depends on repo owners accepting infra update PRs.
> 
> So I’d use a layered model source:
> 
> 1. **Bundled defaults**: shipped with installed Sepo infra.
> 2. **Remote Sepo registry**: optional/default curated JSON from `self-evolving/repo`, fetched at runtime with a short timeout.
> 3. **Repo-owned overrides**: `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`, always highest precedence.
> 
> Precedence should be:
> 
> ```
> bundled Sepo defaults
> < remote Sepo model registry, if enabled and valid
> < AGENT_MODEL_POLICY.default / providers / route_overrides
> < inline workflow route_provider/provider escape hatches
> ```
> 
> Using GitHub raw can work, but I’d make it boring and constrained:
> 
> ```
> https://raw.githubusercontent.com/self-evolving/repo/<stable-ref>/.agent/model-defaults.json
> ```
> 
> Not arbitrary remote URLs by default. Arbitrary URLs are a supply-chain footgun for CI. If we allow them, put them behind an explicit variable like `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY_URL`.
> 
> Suggested config surface:
> 
> * `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY=auto|bundled|remote`
>   
>   * `auto`: try Sepo’s registry, fall back to bundled.
>   * `bundled`: fully deterministic/offline.
>   * `remote`: require remote registry, but still fail closed to bundled unless we intentionally want hard failure.
> * `AGENT_MODEL_REGISTRY_URL`: optional custom registry URL.
> * `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`: local override, still wins.
> 
> Runtime rules:
> 
> * Fetch with a short timeout, maybe 2-5 seconds.
> * Validate schema strictly.
> * Accept only known providers: `codex`, `claude`.
> * Accept only safe model/reasoning tokens using the existing resolver token validation.
> * Log whether the model came from `bundled`, `remote`, or `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`.
> * Never let remote defaults override repo-local `AGENT_MODEL_POLICY`.
> 
> I would not make model names only hardcoded in JS. The better fix is:
> 
> * Move defaults into `.agent/model-defaults.json`.
> * Teach [`resolve-agent-provider`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-agent-provider/resolve-provider.js) to load bundled JSON, then optionally remote JSON, then policy.
> * Keep `agent-update.yml` as the durable infra update path, but let model defaults refresh between infra updates through the remote registry.
> 
> That gives installed repos fresher defaults without forcing frequent Sepo infra updates, while preserving reproducibility and local override control.
>

Implementing this request — tracking in https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/384.

Follow-up after checking the acpx docs and adapter behavior:

The bigger issue is that Codex reasoning is moving into the advertised ACP model id, not a separate `thought_level` setting. The acpx skill/docs say: "For codex, reasoning effort is selected through advertised ACP model ids when the adapter reports model variants."

Under Sepo's current dependency (`acpx 0.6.1`), the built-in Codex adapter path is `@zed-industries/codex-acp@^0.12.0`. That version advertises plain `gpt-5.5` but not `gpt-5.5/xhigh`, and separate `thought_level=xhigh` does not work for `gpt-5.5`.

I tested forcing a newer adapter:

```bash
# project-local deps: acpx@0.6.1 + @zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0
acpx --model gpt-5.5/xhigh codex exec ...
```

With `@zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0`, plain `acpx codex` uses the project-installed adapter and advertises:

```text
gpt-5.5/low
gpt-5.5/medium
gpt-5.5/high
gpt-5.5/xhigh
```

So requiring/pinning the newer `@zed-industries/codex-acp` looks viable, but Sepo also needs to compose the model id before calling acpx. This still fails even with the newer adapter:

```bash
acpx codex set model gpt-5.5 -s <session>
acpx codex set thought_level xhigh -s <session>
```

because `gpt-5.5` alone is no longer an advertised model id in the newer adapter; `gpt-5.5/xhigh` is.

Suggested fix for this PR/follow-up:

1. Add/pin `@zed-industries/codex-acp@0.15.0` in `.agent/package.json` / lockfile so Sepo's acpx uses the newer adapter.
2. For Codex, normalize `model + reasoning_effort` into one model id before passing it to acpx, e.g. `gpt-5.5` + `xhigh` => `gpt-5.5/xhigh`.
3. Do not persist/call `acpx codex set model gpt-5.5` followed by `set thought_level xhigh` for GPT-5.5.

Also note: `codex_version` / installing `@openai/codex` is separate from this; the failing piece is the ACP adapter package that acpx launches.

Closing this as superseded by the focused stack we discussed:

1. #388 updates/pins the Codex ACP adapter and normalizes Codex GPT-5 model+reasoning into effective ACP model ids such as `gpt-5.5/xhigh`.
2. #389 reapplies the pinned provider defaults on top of that fixed naming/runtime foundation.
3. #390 handles default-visible model metadata display.

This avoids merging the current #380 state where Codex was pinned to plain `gpt-5.5` before Sepo knew how to use the newer ACP reasoning model ids.
